summary: The most probable root cause is the aa-sync deploy aa-sync-00633 ('normalize holdings payload v2', 11:19), which likely changed the payload published to portfolio-updates so some messages carry 'positions' instead of 'holdings'. portfolio-consumer rejects them from 11:20:04, causing dead-lettering and redeliveries. aa-sync is the only publisher of the queue and the only change near onset, but this is inferred from timing and topology: the diff is unavailable, no rejected payload was sampled, and logs do not name the producer. Separately, the dead-letter total froze at 2500 from 11:49 while the ready backlog keeps growing and rejections continue, so the DLQ count is no longer a reliable measure of damage. Treat the backlog as the live indicator; the cause of the plateau is unresolved.

hypotheses.statement: The aa-sync deploy aa-sync-00633 ('normalize holdings payload v2', 11:19) changed the payload aa-sync publishes to portfolio-updates so that some messages carry 'positions' instead of 'holdings'; portfolio-consumer's schema validation rejects them from 11:20, causing dead-lettering and redeliveries.
hypotheses.label: medium

supporting.text: aa-sync-00633 ('normalize holdings payload v2') deployed at 11:19, one minute before onset, and was the only aa-sync change in the window.
aa-sync is the only publisher to portfolio-updates, and portfolio-consumer is the only consumer, so the 'positions' messages sit on aa-sync's output path.
The consumer's first ERROR at 11:20:04 is a schema failure reporting unexpected 'positions' (expected 'holdings'). No schema rejection occurred before then, and dead-lettering began at 11:20:00.
The consumer still processes some messages after onset, which fits a subset of messages being rejected rather than a total failure.

contradicting.text: The deploy record has no source or URL, so the diff is unavailable and the link between the note and a holdings-to-positions change is unverified.
aa-sync logs show no errors, no payload-version marker and no instance identifier. Publish lines continue after the deploy but cannot be tied to aa-sync-00633 or to the 'positions' field.
It is unexplained why only about half of users are affected. Nothing shows aa-sync-00633 applies to only some accounts, and the 0.60 error ratio has not been reconciled with the user share.

hypotheses.statement: Separately from the trigger, the dead-letter total froze at 2500 from 11:49 while the ready backlog keeps growing, so dead-lettering has stopped (a DLQ cap or counter/logging stop) or consumers are holding messages unacked or requeuing them; redeliveries of 22-24 per event suggest the same rejected messages are being retried.
hypotheses.label: low

supporting.text: The dead-letter total was still rising (2167 at 11:45, 2417 at 11:48) and then stopped at 2500 from 11:49:05. It stayed at 2500 through 12:19 while the ready backlog grew from 511 to 1201 with 3 consumers still reported.
It is likely that the steady 22-24 redeliveries per event reflect the same rejected messages being retried. This is an assumption not verified against broker counters.

contradicting.text: No broker-side evidence distinguishes a cap, a stopped counter or unacked holding. No policy was found in logs, though that is only an absence in logs and not proof that no policy exists.
The broker error rate is 0, and the redelivery rate did not change at 11:49, so nothing observable changed at the plateau.

hypotheses.statement: A producer other than aa-sync (e.g. portfolio-svc) began publishing a newer payload schema with 'positions' to portfolio-updates at about 11:20, which the consumer rejects.
hypotheses.label: low

supporting.text: It is an unverified assumption that a producer such as portfolio-svc began emitting 'positions'.

contradicting.text: The graph lists aa-sync as the only publisher to portfolio-updates, so portfolio-svc is not shown publishing there.
portfolio-svc error rate stayed low, and its logs show no 'positions' matches. Absence in logs is not proof, though.

hypotheses.statement: portfolio-consumer regressed in its own schema validation so it rejects payloads that are valid, producing the 'positions' rejections.
hypotheses.label: low

contradicting.text: The consumer's only deploy before onset was a 'log level tweak' 30 minutes earlier, and its error rate was at baseline until 11:20. The second consumer deploy came after onset.
Some messages are still processed successfully, and no other change was recorded near onset.

facts.text: Before onset, portfolio-consumer err_rate ranged from 0.002 to 0.004 between 10:50 and 11:19.
portfolio-svc err_rate stayed low across the window (max 0.004), which weakens the idea that the producer is failing outright.
The broker's own error rate on rabbitmq was 0 over the window, which weakens the idea that the broker itself is failing.
The all-service query was complete: total 3, not truncated and not partial. No config, migration, flag or other non-deploy change was returned for any service in the window.
portfolio-consumer had a deploy at 10:50 UTC with the note 'log level tweak', 30 minutes before onset and unlikely to be the trigger.
portfolio-consumer had a second deploy at 12:11 UTC with the note 'metrics label rename'. It occurs after onset and cannot explain it.
aa-sync publishes to the portfolio-updates queue (direct graph edge, not only a synchronous response provider).
The portfolio-updates queue lists aa-sync as its only publisher in the graph.
The portfolio-updates queue lists portfolio-consumer as its only consumer in the graph.

aa-sync deployed aa-sync-00633 at 11:19 UTC, one minute before the reported onset. Only one change was returned for aa-sync in 11:10 to 11:25 across all kinds, and no config, migration or flag change was recorded.
The source and url for aa-sync-00633 are null, so its diff and commit message could not be retrieved and the link between the note and the payload field is unverified.

portfolio-consumer's first schema failure at onset reports an unexpected 'positions' field where it expects 'holdings'. This confirms the consumer sees 'positions' in the payload, but not which service sent it.

aa-sync logged only unrelated INFO 'aa fetch completed' lines between 11:19 and 11:22, with no error, no publish, and no payload-version line. This is consistent with aa-sync-00633 not logging a schema change at deploy time, though the log does not say whether it changed the payload.

portfolio-consumer rps stayed in a narrow band (min 37.62, max 42.754, last 40.376) across the window, with no drop at onset. This weakens the idea that the consumer stopped consuming and supports the idea that it is still pulling messages and failing a subset.
Dead-letter total was still rising just before the plateau, with 2167 at 11:45:07 and 2417 at 11:48:02, so the 2500 value at 11:49:05 is a stop, not a steady state reached earlier.
The dead-letter counter remained at 2500 in its last logged reading at 12:19:46, so it stayed flat for about 30 minutes after 11:49:05 while dead-lettering activity logs were still being written.

Ready depth on portfolio-updates kept growing over the same period, from 511 at 11:45:26 to 1201 at 12:19:17, with 3 consumers still reported. This is a growing backlog while the dead-letter count is flat.
Earlier ready-depth reading: 511 messages ready with 3 consumers at 11:45:26, so the backlog was already growing before the dead-letter plateau.

aa-sync logged only INFO and one unrelated WARN in 11:15–11:25 (no ERROR). Publishing to portfolio-updates continued at 11:15:14, 11:16:01, 11:17:55 and 11:18:00 before the 11:19 deploy window, and one publish line appears at 11:22:49 after it. This does not show a visible aa-sync failure around onset.
No log line mentioning 'policy' exists for rabbitmq across 10:20–12:20, so no max-length or overflow policy was found in logs. This is an absence in logs, not proof that no policy is configured.

A portfolio-svc search for 'positions' between 11:15 and 11:30 returned no matches, so portfolio-svc logs do not show the producer emitting that field. This is an absence in logs, not proof that it was not emitted.
A search for 'v2' in aa-sync INFO logs between 11:18 and 11:25 returned no matches, so there is no log-level version marker from aa-sync at the deploy time.
aa-sync-00633 is the only aa-sync change returned in the window, and it was deployed at 11:19 UTC with the note 'normalize holdings payload v2', one minute before the reported onset.

Redelivery event count: the DEBUG 'redeliver' query returned 60 events with no truncation. My tally is 29 events from 11:20:45 to 11:48:19 and 31 from 11:49:11 to 12:19:43, so the rate did not change at 11:49.
The rabbitmq query for 11:17:00-11:20:10 returned 5 lines, none a rejection. The first dead-letter line is at 11:20:00, after the 11:19:00 deploy window.
portfolio-consumer logged no schema rejection between 11:17:00 and 11:20:10 before onset. Its last pre-onset line was a normal processed update at 11:19:13.
portfolio-consumer still logs successful processing after onset, so some messages are accepted while others are rejected.

aa-sync keeps logging publishes to portfolio-updates after the 11:19 deploy, at 11:22:49, 11:25:00 and 11:28:50. The lines do not name an instance, version or schema, so they cannot separate aa-sync-00633 from other instances.

assumptions.text: The producer (likely portfolio-svc) began emitting a 'positions' field at about 11:20 while the consumer still expects 'holdings'. This is a hypothesis; I have not checked portfolio-svc logs or payloads to confirm it.
The consumer error rate of about 0.60 is a per-message ratio and may not equal the share of affected users (about 50%). The two numbers are not yet reconciled.

The graph lists aa-sync as the only publisher to portfolio-updates, so the earlier hypothesis that portfolio-svc publishes to that queue (E-007) is not supported by this graph data. Portfolio-svc may still be involved, but the dependency data does not show it.
Nothing returned shows that aa-sync-00633 applies only to some accounts. The roughly 50% figure is unexplained by these results.

Steady redelivery counts of about 22-24 suggest the same rejected messages are being requeued and retried repeatedly, rather than new messages being dead-lettered. This fits the flat DLQ counter (E-061) but is not verified against broker unacked or redelivered counters.

actions.text: Roll back aa-sync-00633, or ship a fix so aa-sync publishes 'holdings' again. Confirm that consumer err_rate falls back toward baseline after the rollback.
actions.rationale: It is the only change near onset and aa-sync is the sole publisher to the failing queue. The causal link is still inferred, so verify the effect after rollback.

actions.text: Watch ready depth on portfolio-updates and the consumer error rate directly, not the dead-letter total. Preserve or inspect the rejected and backlogged messages before purging or reprocessing, so no portfolio updates are lost.
actions.rationale: The DLQ counter froze at 2500 at 11:49 while the backlog and rejections continued, so DLQ size understates impact.

actions.text: Sample dead-lettered and accepted messages, including payload fields, app-id and x-death headers. Compare by account to test the 50% split and identify the producer.
actions.rationale: No payload, header or producer data was captured, so the source of 'positions' is unconfirmed.

actions.text: Inspect the broker for the dead-letter exchange and queue configuration, max-length policies, unacked counts and consumer ack rates on portfolio-updates. Check clock skew between hosts.
actions.rationale: This would explain why the dead-letter total froze at 2500 while the backlog grows.

actions.text: Add schema or contract validation for the portfolio-updates payload at publish time, and consider a versioned schema field plus a canary rollout for producer payload changes.
actions.rationale: A producer change dead-lettered messages at the consumer with no pre-release or log-level signal.
